title: Effect of a Single-Head Move
statement: Let $c,C,q\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be a finite bit string, let $s,s'$ be control states, let $h:\{0,\ldots,c\}\to\mathbb{Z}$ be a list of work-head positions, and let $o$ be an output bit string. For an index $i\in\{0,\ldots,c\}$ and a direction $d\in\{-1,0,1\}$, applying the action that moves work head $i$ by $d$ and enters state $s'$ to the configuration with state $s$, head positions $h$, and output $o$ yields the configuration with state $s'$, output $o$, and head positions obtained by replacing $h(i)$ by $h(i)+d$.
hypotheses_covered: $h$ assigns an integer head position to each index from $0$ to $c$
replaced: Let $c, C, q \in \mathbb{N}$, $x$ a bit string, $s, s'$ control states of the unary box enumerator $\mathcal{P}_{c,C}$, $h \colon \{0,\dots,c\} \to \mathbb{Z}$, $o$ an output word, $i \in \{0,\dots,c\}$ and $d \in \{-1,0,1\}$. Applying the action that moves only work head $i$ by $d$ (writing nothing, emitting nothing, input head fixed) and enters $s'$ to $\Gamma_q(s,h,o)$ gives $\Gamma_q(s', h[i \mapsto h(i)+d], o)$; here $\Gamma_q(s,h,o)$ denotes its configuration on input $x$ in control state $s$, with the input head on the blank cell right of the input, every work tape holding $1^q$ in cells $0,\dots,q-1$ and blanks elsewhere, work head $k$ at position $h(k)$, and output $o$, and $h[i \mapsto v]$ is $h$ with its $i$-th entry replaced by $v$.
